callbacks.concept: Force theories to declare their bridge before granting implications
callbacks.summary: When future episodes draw consequences about AI consciousness, uploading, survival, moral status, or meaning, ask which relation is doing the work: identity, realization, constitution, organizational invariance, psychological continuity, bodily continuity, soul-body pairing, divine preservation, resurrection, memory transfer, or generic subjectivity. Do not grant the implication until the bridge is named.

callbacks.concept: Treat moral importance and evidence of consciousness as separate questions
callbacks.summary: Sentience can be morally decisive if present, but moral urgency is not evidence that a system is conscious. Use this distinction when discussing animals, disorders of consciousness, AI welfare, or precautionary policy.

callbacks.concept: Use architecture-sensitive AI indicators rather than fluency or self-report
callbacks.summary: Future AI-consciousness claims should use theory-derived indicators such as recurrence, global availability, self-modeling, agency, world modeling, embodiment, and attention-like control. Fluent language, role-played distress, or claims of self-awareness are not sufficient on their own.

callbacks.concept: Hold substrate independence open with both sides on the table
callbacks.summary: When machine consciousness or uploading returns, preserve both sides: multiple realizability and computational functionalism make nonbiological consciousness possible in principle, while biological naturalism, IIT-style intrinsic causal structure, absent-qualia worries, and embodied or affective views warn that computation or behavior may not be enough.

callbacks.concept: Separate information preservation from subject preservation for uploads
callbacks.summary: An upload claim needs both a consciousness criterion and a personal-identity criterion. A copied pattern, memory set, connectome, or digital successor may preserve information without preserving the original first-person subject.

callbacks.concept: Hold brain dependence as the mainstream constraint on survival claims
callbacks.summary: For afterlife, NDE, reincarnation, resurrection, or survival claims, keep ordinary brain dependence and death by neurologic criteria as the mainstream scientific constraint. Metaphysical possibility and unusual reports do not by themselves establish continuing personal consciousness.

callbacks.concept: Block false balance across implication domains
callbacks.summary: Brain-based neuroscience, analytic metaphysics, AI-welfare forecasting, transhumanist speculation, religious doctrine, and anomalous empirical claims do not have the same evidential status. Preserve live disagreement without presenting every implication as equally supported.

do_not_reexplain: Do not restart the hard problem, Mary, zombies, Nagel's bat, the explanatory gap, or the phenomenal-versus-access distinction; use them as inherited audit tools.
Do not redo the primitive-or-not fork or the warning that correlation is not identity, realization, constitution, grounding, or explanation.
Do not re-enumerate Kuhn's whole taxonomy; name the relevant theory family and move to its implication.
Do not re-list all methodological objections to psi, NDE, and survival evidence; cite the established conditional-and-contested framing.
Do not re-derive multiple realizability, Searle's Chinese Room, biological naturalism, IIT intrinsic-causal-structure framing, or absent-qualia worries from scratch.
Do not re-explain the copy problem, fission, gradual versus destructive replacement, or connectome underspecification every time uploading is mentioned.

durable_concepts.concept: Implications as consequence tests under uncertainty
durable_concepts.summary: Sections 21-25 pivot from theories of consciousness to consequences for value, machine minds, uploading, and death. Their claims are conditional: no downstream implication is stronger than the theory, evidence, and bridge relation that support it.

durable_concepts.concept: Sentience as moral-status bridge, not evidence
durable_concepts.summary: Conscious experience, especially suffering and enjoyment, is a serious ground for moral status. But the ethical importance of sentience must be separated from evidence that a particular animal, patient, AI system, or upload is conscious.

durable_concepts.concept: Meaning questions split into purpose, meaning in life, and value
durable_concepts.summary: Materialism can undercut built-in cosmic purpose without proving nihilism. Cosmic purpose, meaning in life, and objective value are distinct questions, with naturalistic accounts from Flanagan, Kitcher, Wolf, Metz, and empirical psychology addressing only parts of the terrain.

Functionalist and computational views make AI consciousness possible in principle, but current evaluation should look for theory-derived architectural indicators rather than fluency, self-report, user attachment, or role-play.

Multiple realizability and computational functionalism support nonbiological consciousness in principle, while Searle, biological naturalism, IIT-style intrinsic structure, absent-qualia cases, embodiment, affect, metabolism, and homeostasis preserve serious objections.

durable_concepts.concept: Uploading requires both consciousness and identity criteria
durable_concepts.summary: Strong virtual immortality requires a digital system to be phenomenally conscious and to preserve the original subject rather than merely create a successor. Functional organization, memories, personality, and connectome structure are not enough unless a theory explains why they preserve first-person continuity.

durable_concepts.concept: Copy problem and technical underspecification constrain uploads
durable_concepts.summary: Pattern copying, fission cases, and destructive scan-and-copy scenarios pressure numerical identity. Whole-brain emulation also remains underspecified because a connectome may omit synaptic strengths, neuromodulators, glia, molecular traces, metabolism, development, embodiment, and brain-body regulation.

durable_concepts.concept: Brain dependence is the survival default constraint
durable_concepts.summary: Brain damage, anesthesia, neurodegeneration, and death by neurologic criteria make ordinary continuing mental life after total brain failure scientifically difficult. Dualist, idealist, theistic, NDE, reincarnation, and resurrection routes must be tagged by their epistemic status.

durable_concepts.concept: Nonpersonal continuity is not ordinary survival
durable_concepts.summary: Clark's generic subjective continuity and block-universe eternalism offer naturalistic continuity frames, but they do not preserve the dead person's memories, projects, relationships, or first-person point of view.

The cluster mixes mainstream science, active philosophy, formal theory, speculation, religious metaphysics, and weakly evidenced anomalous claims. These domains must remain live but epistemically ranked.

open_tensions: Whether architecture-derived AI indicators can become an accepted consciousness meter rather than a theory-laden conditional checklist remains open.

Whether functional organization is sufficient for phenomenal consciousness, or whether biology, intrinsic causal structure, embodiment, affect, or noncomputational features are required, remains unsettled.
Whether precautionary AI-welfare policy should treat present systems as plausible sentience candidates or only prepare for future systems remains unresolved.
Whether psychological continuity is enough for personal survival, or whether numerical identity requires a further fact that copying cannot preserve, remains open.
Whether whole-brain emulation can capture enough neural, bodily, developmental, and environmental detail to preserve a subject remains technically underspecified.
Whether NDE, reincarnation, and survival literatures will mature into robust independently verified evidence or remain weak relative to their implications is unresolved.
Whether materialism undercuts cosmic purpose while still leaving objective value and meaning in life defensible remains contested.
Whether nonpersonal continuity views offer meaningful consolation or merely change the subject from survival to continuity of experience somewhere is open.
recurring_distinctions: Theory of consciousness versus downstream implication.
Moral importance of sentience versus evidence that a being is sentient.
Fluent behavior and self-report versus phenomenal experience.
Architecture-sensitive indicator versus accepted consciousness meter.
Psychological continuity versus numerical personal identity.
Brain dependence as mainstream constraint versus metaphysical possibility.
Cosmic purpose versus meaning in life versus objective value.
Metaphysical or theological possibility versus empirical confirmation.
Nonpersonal continuity versus ordinary personal survival.
thesis: This cluster pivots from consciousness theories to consequences under uncertainty: meaning, moral status, AI consciousness, virtual immortality, and survival beyond death. Its durable lesson is bridge discipline. Implications matter, but each one breaks unless the theory states what relation, criterion, or evidence licenses it.
